title: Board update prep notes
content:
Purpose: rough scratchpad for preparing the 20–30 minute board update. Not polished; use as source for slide copy and CEO talking points. Leave comments inline — I will consolidate by Mon 3/16.

Topline framing (one sentence options)
- Option A: "Redwood delivered predictable, lower-cost inference at scale this quarter while expanding private deployment pilots with three regulated customers."
- Option B (more conservative): "We hit important operational milestones and validated product-market fit for Dedicated; macro demand remains uneven and we are prioritizing unit economics improvements."
- Which tone? preference from CEO: confident but not overpromising.

Key metrics to surface (draft numbers — confirm with finance before slides)
- Hosted API revenue growth: +34% QoQ (verify MRR vs usage revenue split)
- Dedicated contract ARR closed: $1.2M incremental (3 deals); pipeline: $7.4M (90d weighted)
- Private pilots: 3 active (healthcare, fintech, gov) — expected conversion window: 6–9 months
- Latency SLO attainment: 98.6% across global regions (see SRE report INF-2345)
- Unit cost per 1k tokens: target down 12% YoY (note: compaction from Optimize rollout is main driver)

Narrative structure (recommended)
1) Quick wins & operational health (latency, incident rate down, Dedicated throughput)
2) Commercial momentum (notable logos, pipeline, pilot traction)
3) Product roadmap highlights & risk mitigations (Private delivery, model onboarding, Optimize features)
4) Ask of the board (hiring authority, sales support intros, fundraising cadence if relevant)

Sensitive items / redlines to be explicit about
- Cash runway : not urgent per latest finance check but slower enterprise conversion could push conservative hiring plan. We should avoid exact runway number in board slides until finance signs off.
- Incident recap: 2/17 partial degradation — root cause: autoscale race, partial KV cache corruption. Our remediation plan is in progress; include timeline and mitigation (fallback routing) but keep deep technical details to appendix.
- Pricing discussion: considering small price increase for premium SLA on hosted API. Need to surface potential customer pushback and go/no-go criteria.

Draft Q&A (likely board questions and short answers)
Q: Are Dedicated deals repeatable?
A: Early signs are yes — three deals from mid-market product teams, typical conversion drivers: predictable throughput, compliance, and cost guarantees. Pipeline shows multiple 'near-term' opportunities at similar deal sizes. Sales cycle still 3–6 months.

Q: How sticky are Private pilots?
A: Pilots are sticky when we integrate KMS and provide audit logs; two pilots have already requested a 12-month roadmap; conversion depends on SOC 2 / HIPAA readiness and a finalized pricing model.

Q: Any model quality regressions with quantized/optimized variants?
A: We have regression monitoring and a rollback policy. Small quality delta for some LLMs in rare cases; we are adding prompt-level evaluation hooks to detect regressions earlier.

Q: Do we need more capital?
A: Not immediately. We are tracking enterprise conversion cadence; if pipeline conversion stalls, we may propose a smaller bridge. Finance will present sensitivity analysis in the appendix.

Suggested CEO talking points (short bullets)
- Thank board, quick 30s on mission and market — supply predictable inference for builders
- Call out operational improvements that preserve customer SLAs (latency, degradation handling)
- Highlight 1–2 customer stories (name redacted if sensitive) that show value of Dedicated/private options
- Present clear ask: 3 hires (sales AE for Mid-Market, TPM for Private, SRE for infra hardening) — with rationale and cost implication

Appendix ideas (for board packet)
- Incident timeline & remediation (concise)
- Top-of-funnel metrics and pipeline waterfall (monthly cadence)
- Detailed cost-per-token trends and Optimize impact simulation (before/after)
- Legal/compliance checklist for Private conversions (SOC/HIPAA items)

Open items / TODOs (who/when)
- Finance to verify revenue/ARR numbers and confirm runway language (Alisha) — due Wed 3/13
- SRE to provide short incident timeline and updated SLO numbers + graph (Marco) — due Thu 3/14
- Sales to extract 3 short customer vignettes for slides (no PII) — due Fri 3/15
- Draft slide deck: start from last board deck; reuse 'metrics' and 'incidents' slides, add new 'Dedicated wins' slide (Izumi to coordinate) — draft by Mon 3/16

Rough slide order (for design)
1) Title & mission one-liner
2) Topline metrics snapshot (1 slide)
3) Operational health + incident summary (1 slide)
4) Commercial momentum & key deals (1 slide)
5) Product roadmap & risks (1 slide)
6) Ask & hires (1 slide)
7) Appendix (incidents, pipeline details, finance sensitivity)

Stylistic notes for slides/talking points
- Keep language plain, avoid engineering jargon in topline slides
- Use one metric per visual; avoid cramming data
- For sensitive threads, use high-level bullets and put specifics in appendix

Random scratch ideas to consider
- Quick 90-second customer video or quote in slide 4 — does sales have recordings?
- Small 'walkthrough' of fallback routing in appendix to show resiliency tech without deep code detail

End notes: This doc is a live scratchpad. My goal: finalize slide copy by 3/16 and circulate for one round of comments. If anyone wants to jump on a 30-minute prep call, ping me (Izumi) — I'll set up time slots next Tue/Thu morning.
